title: 30T80 corn (Pioneer 30T80): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: 30T80 corn is a yellow GM hybrid corn variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: 30T80 corn is a yellow GM hybrid corn variety, also sold or known as Pioneer 30T80 or P30T80. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2008 as NSIC 2008 GMCn 26. Pioneer Hi Bred Agricultural Technologies bred it. Its record notes 6.22 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Pioneer 30T80 or P30T80, this is the same corn. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [corn variety finder](/crop-varieties/corn), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Pagtatanim ng mais, step by step](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Its average yield of 6.22 t/ha trails the average of its group, 8.13. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer).

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 6.22 t/ha in NSIC trials, 5.05 t/ha listed by DA Region 2.
Rated resistant to corn borer, earworm and leaf diseases.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a long running Pioneer hybrid that was on DA Region 2's recommended list with seed at the Ilagan station. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant 30T80 corn

The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country in both the wet and the dry season. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.a: Yes. Pioneer 30T80 is another name for 30T80, registered as NSIC 2008 GMCn 26. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows 6.22 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.
The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country in both the wet and the dry season. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of 30T80?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
